subject: Trial extension: voucher top-up vs. time extension — ops insurance question
messages:
From: Evan Cross <evan.cross@nuvohealth.com>

Cc: Samira Patel <samira.patel@nuvohealth.com>

Subject: Request: short trial top-up and surge protection options

Hi Hiro / Jordan,

Quick context: we're mid-pilot on Redwood (started Mar 10) and the team wants to extend the evaluation to finish a second integration and an internal load test. We expect another 2–3 weeks of active testing. Current blockers are:
- We burned through our test tokens faster than expected due to integration replays.
- We have concerns about a short burst for load testing — would appreciate a guarantee or insurance for capacity/surge so our SREs can run the tests without throttling.

Two quick asks:
1) Can you outline options for a short extension (3 weeks) versus a voucher/credit top-up (token-based) and the tradeoffs (cost, SLA, throttling behavior)?
2) Do you offer a temporary ops/surge insurance add-on (engineering on-call, reserved burst lanes) and how is that priced?

Goal: decide today so we can schedule the load test for next week.

I've CC'd Samira from procurement — she'll handle PO if we move forward. Attaching the latest SOW we use for internal approvals.

Thanks,
Evan
Evan Cross
Director, Platform Engineering | NuvoHealth
Evan.Cross@nuvohealth.com

From: hiro_tanaka@redwood.com
To: Evan Cross <evan.cross@nuvohealth.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short trial top-up and surge protection options

Evan — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer: yes, we can do both voucher top-ups and short time-box extensions; we also offer a temporary surge/ops insurance add-on.

High-level tradeoffs (quick):
- Time extension (add X days to your existing trial window): simplest operationally — your sessions keep the same routing and no token accounting changes. Downside: we reserve instance slots for the extended window which can be slightly more expensive if you don't fully use it.
- Voucher / token top-up: flexible; you get a pool of tokens/credits you can spend over the current window. Lower risk for us and you only pay for what you use, but there are scenarios where heavy short bursts may face queueing if capacity is constrained.

Surge / ops insurance: we can enable a "surge lane" for your account for the duration (3 weeks) that reduces the probability of queueing during load tests and includes a named on-call engineer for 8x5 coverage. Pricing is a flat fee + small per-token surcharge during the surge period.

Two options we'd propose immediately:
A) 3-week time extension: flat fee $9,000 (includes minor reserved capacity bump).
B) Voucher top-up: $6,500 credit (applies to tokens) + optional surge insurance add-on $2,400 for 3 weeks. If you pick B and later convert to Dedicated within 60 days we will credit 50% of the voucher towards the committed capacity.

If you can share a short forecast (expected peak tokens/day for the load test) we can recommend A vs. B and size the surge lane. I've attached a very small usage extract from our dashboard to help (pilot_usage_summary.csv).

I'll let Jordan follow up with a pricing table and contractual next steps.

— Hiro
Hiro Tanaka
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference
hiro.tanaka@redwood.com

Attachment: pilot_usage_summary.csv (csv stub)

Thanks Hiro — useful framing. Quick numbers from our side for the next test:
- Expected steady-state: ~250k tokens/day
- Load test peak (30 minutes): ~2.5M tokens total during the window
- Duration of peak: roughly 30–45 minutes

Preference: voucher top-up + surge insurance if that guarantees the load window will run without significant throttling. We prefer paying only for what we use but can't risk a stopped test.

Can you send a short one-pager that explains the operational difference (what happens if capacity is constrained with voucher vs. time extension) and a simple pricing grid so I can brief procurement (Samira). If voucher+insurance is the path, Samira will route PO.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Evan

Evan / Samira — quick follow-up with a clear pricing grid and recommended route. Prices below are illustrative and written to be executable today.

Option 1 — Voucher (preferred for flexibility):
- 600k token voucher: $6,500 (good for current window)
- Surge insurance add-on (3 weeks): $2,400 — includes named on-call engineer 8x5 + reserved burst lane up to 3x your steady-state for 1 hour continuous.
- If you convert to a 6-month Dedicated commitment within 60 days: 50% of voucher credited toward first invoice.

Option 2 — Time extension (3 weeks):
- Flat fee: $9,000 (we reserve capacity to match your historical 95th percentile). Includes one scheduled maintenance-free load window (up to 45 minutes).

Tradeoffs recap:
- Voucher: pay-as-you-go, more efficient if you only run one big load window; slight chance of queueing without surge insurance.
- Time extension: operationally simplest, guaranteed reserved window but higher upfront cost if you don't use it.

DocuSign for the short addendum (when you confirm) and a short SOW for the surge lane are ready. We can also do a hybrid: 300k voucher + 1-week time extension if you'd like to split risk.

If Samira is ready, route PO to finance@redwood.com and we will countersign same business day. DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/ABCDEF123456

— Jordan
